RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 35

An all-male panel is not evidence of bias by itself — it's common in economics and reflects the field's demographics more than any decision. On its own it proves nothing, and leading with it makes you look like you're reaching.

Your stronger facts are concrete: a completed PhD versus an unfinished one, six papers versus two, four years of teaching — and silence on a request for written reasons, which public universities are usually obliged to provide.

So: push hard on the unanswered request, in writing, citing the relevant rule or statute. Mention panel composition only as background if the stated reasons turn out to be vague, shifting, or weight "industry experience" that was never in the advertised criteria.
